How this was recorded

These are not mockups. Native clips come from the exported Linux build running on an Xvfb display with Mesa llvmpipe; Godot's --fixed-fps 24 forced a deterministic 1/24 s timestep while Tools/record_media.py captured the actual viewport of every rendered frame to PNG and injected real keyboard/mouse input with xdotool. Those PNG sequences were encoded to H.264 MP4 with ffmpeg. The browser clip is a live X11 capture of the exported WebAssembly build in Chromium with SwiftShader WebGL. Clip lengths in this page are parsed from the MP4 mvhd atom at build time, so they stay correct even without ffprobe.

Honest limits: this is an original indie-scale football game, not FIFA/PES. Characters, kits, crowd and stadium are procedural; there are no licensed teams, likenesses, commentary audio, motion capture, career mode, matchmaking/accounts, VAR or skill-move system. Online play with friends is implemented (room codes, reconnect, host migration, rollback prediction). The web edition is a reduced GDScript 5-a-side build because Godot 4 cannot export C# to Web. macOS and Android packages are unsigned and iOS needs a Mac with Xcode.
Original code, meshes, shaders, names and UI - MIT licensed. No FIFA/PES/eFootball assets, branding, likenesses, kits, audio or proprietary code were used.
